sources.title: User clarification
sources.locator: Conversation: target is the Website tab, not the landing page

users.description: A CAM or property manager editing one community website; the role and route gates are explicit, but direct research evidence is unavailable.
A property manager who may move between portfolio and community contexts; this audience is implied by the PM nav and route comments, not validated research.

tasks.description: Edit the selected community website content and branding while staying oriented in the community workspace.
See how the current draft will appear publicly without leaving the editing context.
Understand what is draft versus live, then publish or discard changes with confidence.
Move between community work and portfolio management without the global navigation feeling replaced unexpectedly.

claims.text: The Website editor should preserve a stable community workspace navigation model when the Website tab is selected.
The repository already has an authenticated route that renders the same public-site layout inside a preview surface.
The editor distinguishes local draft changes from a global publish action and supports discard/conflict/error outcomes.
The redesign should align with PropertyPro semantic tokens, Florida Modern warmth, spacing, focus, touch target, and motion rules.

assumptions.description: The Website tab refers to the authenticated editor page, with public preview as a companion surface rather than a separate redesign target.

validation.hypothesis: A split editor/preview workspace will address the user's Website-tab complaint without changing public-site rendering behavior.
killCriteria: The user identifies the public-site preview as the only target.
The user needs a different role or route context than the authenticated Website editor.

assumptions.description: The preferred direction is to keep community navigation visible and make portfolio controls secondary or explicit rather than swapping the whole sidebar.

validation.hypothesis: A stable community shell will reduce the feeling that clicking Website changes the app's mode unexpectedly.
killCriteria: Operators prefer the PM-only nav for Website editing after reviewing the alternative.
The route architecture makes a stable shell materially unsafe or misleading.

unknowns.description: It is not confirmed whether the preview should be persistent side-by-side, a collapsible panel, or a separate tab on the Website editor.
unknowns.rationale: The mockup can compare the side-by-side hypothesis; implementation should follow explicit review.

unknowns.description: It is not confirmed whether a PM needs to retain portfolio-level controls while editing a single community site.
unknowns.rationale: The stable-shell direction preserves community context and can expose a clearly labeled portfolio escape hatch.

unknowns.description: The amount of existing site content and the preferred default open sections are unknown for real communities.
unknowns.rationale: The demo uses representative sections and progressive disclosure rather than assuming a final content volume.

directionCriteria.description: Selecting Website leaves the operator oriented in the same community workspace rather than replacing the global navigation without explanation.
directionCriteria.measurement: Browser walkthrough and human review confirm the selected Website screen keeps a stable sidebar model or makes any context transition explicit and reversible.

directionCriteria.description: The operator can understand the relationship between editor changes and the public-site result without repeatedly losing place or opening unrelated surfaces.
directionCriteria.measurement: A reviewer can locate the active editor section, see a representative preview, and identify the preview action at desktop and mobile widths.

directionCriteria.description: Local Save actions and global Publish Website are visually distinct, with draft/live status visible near the page title and publish affordance.
directionCriteria.measurement: A reviewer can answer what is saved locally, what is pending, and what will go live without reading implementation details.

directionCriteria.description: The redesign uses existing PropertyPro semantic surfaces, warm brand intent, spacing rhythm, focus behavior, touch targets, and restrained elevation.
directionCriteria.measurement: Each major visual treatment maps to the documented system and the mockup remains readable without decorative gradients, unsupported metrics, or color-only status.

auditOnlyException: This registry is evidence-bounded: it records the clarified target, repository facts, explicit assumptions, and unanswered questions without fabricating user research, analytics, customer proof, or product requirements.
